subject: Post-demo ops integration: latency, throughput & residency (SaaSCo)
body:
From: Naomi Feldman <naomi.feldman@redwood.com>
To: Emily Stone <emily.stone@saasco.com>, Victor Gomez <victor.gomez@saasco.com>
Cc: Rishi Malhotra <rishi.malhotra@redwood.com>, Grace O'Connor <grace.oconnor@redwood.com>, Marcus Lin <marcus.lin@redwood.com>
Date: Mon, 26 Apr 2027 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Post-demo ops integration: latency, throughput & residency (SaaSCo)

Hi Emily / Victor —

Thanks again for taking the demo earlier. Quick post-call recap focused on the operational requirements you asked us to confirm for procurement and engineering alignment. I attached a draft SLO matrix and a suggested SLA doc for your legal team (SaaSCo-SLO-Matrix-v1.xlsx, redwood-sla-draft.pdf).

Key items we captured on the call:
- Latency targets (P95/P99) by region. You asked for P95 ~100–150ms for US interactive flows and <=200ms for EU, with APAC acceptable up to 250ms for the first phase.
- Throughput & concurrency: nominal steady-state of 600 requests/sec with burst expected to 2k req/sec for short windows. Per-session concurrency: ~12–20 per user peak.
- Streaming: some features will use streaming token-by-token outputs; expected average stream token rate ~50–80 tokens/sec per open connection.
- Regional routing/data residency: EU traffic must be processed and logged in EU-only infrastructure; APAC must prefer APAC region with US fallback only if APAC capacity exhausted, per the fallthrough policy you described.
- Logging & audit: 1 year retention, access via customer KMS for encryption keys, logs hashed/partitioned by customer id.

Questions / asks for SaaSCo to confirm:
1) Please confirm the hard max for P95 latency per region you need for the production SLA (US / EU / APAC).
2) Are the burst windows 2k req/sec acceptable as a committed peak we should provision for, or do you prefer an autoscaling billing model for bursts?
3) For APAC fallback, do you require an explicit notice period before routing to US (e.g., 10 minutes) or is automatic failover acceptable?

Next steps (proposed):
- We (Redwood) will provide a short ops appendix that maps each SLO to the technical controls (prefix KV cache, batching profiles, quantization options, routing policy).
- Rishi will propose a rough capacity table (GPUs, instances, concurrency) and cost delta between dedicated reservation vs hosted burst model.
- If you confirm numbers above, we can produce an SLA-ready PDF for your procurement/legal to start review.

Owner: Naomi (sales-eng) — I copied infra & product for visibility.

Thanks,
Naomi Feldman
Enterprise AE | Redwood Inference
naomi.feldman@redwood.com
+1 (415) 555-0123

-----Original attachments: SaaSCo-SLO-Matrix-v1.xlsx (spreadsheet), redwood-sla-draft.pdf (PDF)

From: Emily Stone <emily.stone@saasco.com>
To: Naomi Feldman <naomi.feldman@redwood.com>
Cc: Victor Gomez <victor.gomez@saasco.com>
Date: Tue, 27 Apr 2027 09:03:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Post-demo ops integration: latency, throughput & residency (SaaSCo)

Naomi —

Thanks for the clear recap and the attachments. A couple clarifications from our side before we punt this to procurement:  

1) EU residency: SaaSCo requires that both inference and logs for EU customer data stay within EU boundaries. No processing in US is allowed except for aggregated metrics (no customer-identifiable logs). Is that something Redwood can guarantee?

2) APAC routing: We operate in Japan and Australia. For the first 6 months we want APAC routed to the Tokyo/Sydney region. If capacity limits are reached we are comfortable with a controlled failover to US but need an automated alert and a 10-minute holdoff before failover to allow our ops to react.

3) Streaming: We will have websockets open for user sessions with an average of 65 tokens/sec and spikes up to 120 tokens/sec. Will that materially change session concurrency assumptions?

Also — can Rishi or infra provide a one-page note that maps how prefix caching and batching will affect P95 for interactive streaming? That will help our SRE team.

Emily
Emily Stone
Head of Platform Engineering | SaaSCo
emily.stone@saasco.com

------------------------------------------------------------------------
From: Naomi Feldman <naomi.feldman@redwood.com>
To: Emily Stone <emily.stone@saasco.com>, Victor Gomez <victor.gomez@saasco.com>
Cc: Rishi Malhotra <rishi.malhotra@redwood.com>, Grace O'Connor <grace.oconnor@redwood.com>, Marcus Lin <marcus.lin@redwood.com>, Priyom Das <priyom.das@redwood.com>
Date: Tue, 27 Apr 2027 11:08:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Post-demo ops integration: latency, throughput & residency (SaaSCo)

Emily —

Appreciate the details; all good asks. High-level answers below; Rishi has agreed to add the caching/batching note you requested.

1) EU residency: we offer an EU-dedicated tenancy option (Private deployment / VPC) that keeps inference and logs in-region and under your KMS. That lifecycle will satisfy the EU-only requirement. For hosted customers we can also provide EU-hosted instances with strict routing policies and KMS integration — we will flag any exceptions (e.g., scheduled maintenance or cross-region DR drills) in the SLA appendix.

2) APAC routing: we can implement a failover policy with a configurable holdoff (10 minutes is fine). We will emit an automated alert to your webhook and SRE pager prior to any cross-region failover.

3) Streaming rates: 65 tokens/sec average with 120 spikes is within expected profile, but streaming increases per-connection resource usage (KV cache residency and per-stream token scheduling). Suggested starting concurrency per GPU is roughly 10–14 concurrent streaming sessions (depending on model size). We'll propose a mixed pool with streaming-optimized instances to avoid impacting batched generation throughput.

Next steps from Redwood:
- Rishi: 1-pager on caching/batching effects and estimated instance table.
- Marcus: rough cost delta for Dedicated EU tenancy vs hosted EU routing.
- Naomi: update SLA appendix to include the 10-minute APAC failover holdoff clause and EU KMS wording.

Can we set a 30-minute follow-up on Thu 4/29 at 09:00 PT to walk procurement through the SLA language?

Thanks,
Naomi

From: Rishi Malhotra <rishi.malhotra@redwood.com>
To: Emily Stone <emily.stone@saasco.com>, Naomi Feldman <naomi.feldman@redwood.com>
Cc: Grace O'Connor <grace.oconnor@redwood.com>, Marcus Lin <marcus.lin@redwood.com>, Priyom Das <priyom.das@redwood.com>
Date: Wed, 28 Apr 2027 08:34:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Post-demo ops integration: latency, throughput & residency (SaaSCo)

Emily / Naomi —

Attached is the 1-pager you requested: short note on prefix KV caching, continuous batching behavior, and expected P95 improvement for interactive streaming. Summary bullets here:  

- Prefix/KV cache: for repeated conversational traffic caching can reduce token-generation backend time by ~20–40% depending on prompt overlap. Cache warmup policy: we can pre-warm with a seed set you provide.
- Continuous batching: non-streaming requests can be batched with latency heat thresholds; for interactive flows we keep batch sizes small to prioritize latency (batch target: 8–16 tokens depending on model).
- Streaming impact: per-session scheduling means P95 gains are more modest vs batch; expect 10–25% improvement from caching for streaming flows.

Technical clarifications I need from your SREs to firm numbers:  
A) Typical prompt length (tokens) for interactive flows (median + 95th).
B) Expected distribution of streaming vs non-streaming calls (percentage).

If you can share those two items, I will produce a small capacity table (GPUs / concurrency / expected P95) and a recommended instance mix.

Regards,
Rishi Malhotra
Sr. Infra Engineer | Redwood Inference
rishi.malhotra@redwood.com

Attachments: Redwood-prefix-cache-note.pdf (1 page)

------------------------------------------------------------------------
From: Emily Stone <emily.stone@saasco.com>
To: Naomi Feldman <naomi.feldman@redwood.com>, Rishi Malhotra <rishi.malhotra@redwood.com>
Cc: Victor Gomez <victor.gomez@saasco.com>
Date: Wed, 28 Apr 2027 10:45:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Post-demo ops integration: latency, throughput & residency (SaaSCo)

Naomi / Rishi —

Thanks — this is exactly what we needed. Short answers below to help your sizing:  

A) Prompt length: median interactive prompt ~120 tokens, 95th ~600 tokens.
B) Distribution: at launch we expect ~70% streaming sessions, 30% non-streaming (bulk API).

We confirm EU-only processing & logs for EU customers and the 10-minute APAC holdoff. Procurement will take the SLA draft and the dedicated tenancy pricing you provide and follow up with redlines.

We can join Thu 4/29 09:00 PT — Victor and I will be there. Please share the calendar invite and the updated SLA appendix before EOD Thu 4/28 so procurement has something to review before the call.

Best,
Emily
